content.confidence: 3: You are fairly confident in your assessment. It is possible that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work. Math/other details were not carefully checked.
content.summary_of_the_paper: In this work, the authors propose NetBooster to improve the performance of small networks based on expanding and contraction strategies. This strategy first expands each/some layer(s) of a given network into multi-layer blocks so that it can learn complex features and then contracts the expanded layers by gradually removing the non-linear layers from the expanded ones to recover efficiency. For expansion, it does it on the commonly used blocks, e.g. the basic and bottleneck blocks in ResNet, and uniformly selects the layers to expand. For expansion ratio, it is set to be 6 used in other work.  For contraction, it slightly revises ReLU so that it can gradually remove the non-linearity in ReLU.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths: 
There are main two contributions in this work. 
1)This work proposes a very general training strategy to improve the performance of small networks via the proposed expanding and contraction strategy. 

2)For technique, the contribution is revised ReLU so that it can gradually remove the non-linearity in ReLU. For other expansions,  e.g. block and layer selection,  the author does not design special methods, for contraction, it can follow the standard one. 


Weaknesses:
1)The proposed  method is slightly incremental, since NetAug (Cai et al., 2021) actually does a similar training strategy. The difference is that NetAug augments the width, while this work extends this to augmentation of both width and depth.  But the main idea is exactly the same. 


2)To handle depth augmentation, the only difference between this work and NetAug (Cai et al., 2021), the technique contribution is to revises ReLU so that  it can gradually remove the non-linearity in ReLU. For other expansion,  e.g. block and layer selection,  the author does not design special methods, for contraction, it can follow the standard one. So this results in another issue, incremental technique contributions. 


3)For experimental results, in most cases, the proposed method only improves NetAug by about 0.2-0.4% which is a small improvement, especially the baseline performance is not high (about 50-70% accuracy). But the method in this one needs to augment depth and width, while  NetAug only augments the width. Moreover, this naturally brings more extra computational costs. So for a fair comparison, the authors should also compare the total training cost for all experiments.

4)For some tables, e.g. Table 2, the authors do not compare with NetAug .

5)whether this strategy can also be applied to other activations, such as the widely used GELU  and ELU which have very different learning functions from RELU.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
For writing, most parts of this work are well-written and clear.  

For novelty, the novelty of this work is not high since it is very similar to the existing one. For technique contribution, it is incremental, since the main contribution comes from the revision of ReLU so that it can gradually remove the non-linearity in ReLU.
content.summary_of_the_review: Overall, this work provides some good empirical results. But it fails to provide good new insights and superior techniques.
content.correctness: 3: Some of the paper’s claims have minor issues. A few statements are not well-supported, or require small changes to be made correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.

content.confidence: 5: You are absolutely certain about your assessment. You are very familiar with the related work and checked the math/other details carefully.
content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes Netbooster, a framework to first expand a given network and then remove non-linearities to make it compact. It targets tiny ML networks and datasets.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
The paper has following strengths:

1. Authors have conducted comprehensive experiments to show consistent improvements over existing methods in tinyML space like NetAug. 

2. Good and useful ablations are presented.

3. Paper is well-written and easy to understand.


The paper has following weaknesses:

1. The major weakness of this work is that the idea has already been done (although the idea itself is interesting). There are at least two existing papers that have done a very similar (and slightly better) idea for image classification (that too for larger networks like EfficientNets/MobileNet-V2): DepthShrinker (ICML 2022, https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.00843) and Restructurable Activation Networks (RANs, arXiv 2022: https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.08562). The ICML paper appeared online in June, so I expect a head-to-head comparison under the same settings. The idea in RANs is quite similar to Netbooster but RANs are slightly better since they learn the alpha parameters instead of naively scaling them up and also propose a generic search space. Learning of non-linearity pruning also happens in DepthShrinker so I am curious to see how authors’ model compares to DepthShrinker. Since RANs are more general, they beat DepthShrinker significantly. However, because RANs appeared online only a few weeks before ICLR deadline, I do not expect authors to provide a comparison against RANs. Anyways, the authors must discuss both DepthShrinker and RANs in detail in related work (and provide a quantitative comparison against DepthShrinker in experiments). Please also remove the first contribution (in intro) claims like “first to do this idea” since there are multiple papers that do this.

2. The authors present a lot of description around how the Netbooster approach can improve the feature representations and alleviate underfitting issues. However, no theoretical or empirical arguments are provided to support any of this. Doesn’t the overall learning capacity and expressive power of the network become the same as the original compact model when you get rid of the non-linearities? Since we are seeing improvements in experiments, the proposed technique may be altering the optimization landscape. It is well-known that linear overparameterization accelerates training convergence (see https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.06509). Hence, it is possible that the actual reasons for improvement in accuracy are completely different from what authors are hypothesizing. I can still appreciate this work as an empirical contribution. However, the authors must make sure they clearly indicate what they are speculating vs. what can be proven (this is unclear throughout most of the paper). For example, if you think Netbooster way of training improves underfitting, then prove (or at least somehow empirically show) that training a model this way can improve its expressive power and thus the model is able to fit the function better (I do not think it does because the overall structure of the final network stays constant in depth and width and also in terms of number of non-linear units). If the expressive power of the network does not change, then how can it fix the underfitting issue? Similar thing applies to all other supporting claims (improved feature representation, etc., that could be empirically shown using techniques like GradCAM, etc.).

3. Why is there no NetAug and NetAug+KD in Table 2?

4. Successive convolutions being combined into a single one was also done in several existing works. For example, see ExpandNets: https://arxiv.org/abs/1811.10495, SESR: https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.09404.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper is clearly written and experiments are comprehensive. Novelty is low because the idea already exists (however, one of the two existing papers for this idea should be considered concurrent).
content.summary_of_the_review: The paper has some novelty issues and some potential technical correctness issues. This can be a useful work from an empirical standpoint (particularly for tinyML applications). However, the above two points need to be significantly improved.
content.correctness: 2: Several of the paper’s claims are incorrect or not well-supported.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.

content.summary_of_the_paper: In this work, the authors proposed a pipeline to deal with balancing the model performance and the model size for deep neural networks. The whole approach is mainly composed of two stages. The first stage is to expand the network for better learning performance. The second stage is to improve the efficiency by removing non-linear layers. The authors have evaluated the proposed approach on image classification and object detection tasks. The results have demonstrated the feasibility of proposed approach on solving lower performance issue with efficient network architecture.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
1.	The whole approach utilized the popular model structure and approaches in the design, e.g., utilizing inverted residual block from mobile v2 for block insert. It is easier to understand the whole workflow.
2.	The experimental results demonstrate the improvement over the compared results. 

Weakness:
1.	Transformer related architecture is becoming popular now days and always achieve better performance than general CNN based framework. Can this approach apply to transformer?
2.	The authors have listed the performance comparison, but did not find the comparison related with the parameter reduction. 
3.     There is not automatic way to choose the expansion ratio which may limit its application to the new framework design.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper writing quality is ok, Although there is no new architecture proposed in this work, this work do propose a new workflow design for dealing with the lower performance problem in tiny deep learning framework. The results can be reproducible.
content.summary_of_the_review: I would like to give the borderline. The authors have listed the performance gain over other benchmarks. However, parameter reduction is also an important part for this area.
